2026-04-15 03:00 KST

## CRITICAL Issues (3)

   - channels.telegram.groupPolicy = "open" with tools.elevated enabled

   - Fix: Set groupPolicy="allowlist" and keep elevated allowlists tight

   - channels.telegram.groupPolicy = "open"
   - Risky contexts:
     * agents.defaults (sandbox=off; runtime=[exec, process]; fs=[read, write, edit, apply_patch]; fs.workspaceOnly=false)
     * agents.list.main (same configuration)
   - Prompt injection can trigger command/file actions in these contexts
   - Fix: Use tools.profile="messaging" for open groups, set tools.fs.workspaceOnly=true, and use agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all"

3. Telegram Group Policy Open Without Allowlist
   - groupPolicy="open" with no channels.telegram.groups allowlist
   - Any group can add and ping (mention-gated)
   - Fix: Set channels.telegram.groupPolicy="allowlist" + channels.telegram.groupAllowlist or configure channels.telegram.groups

## WARN Issues (4)

1. Reverse Proxy Headers Not Trusted
   - gateway.trustedProxies is empty

   - Fix: Set gateway.trustedProxies to proxy IPs or keep Control UI local-only

2. Auto-Allow Skills Enabled for Exec Approvals
   - defaults.autoAllowSkills enabled
   - Widens host exec trust beyond explicit allowlists
   - Fix: Disable autoAllowSkills and keep manual allowlists tight

3. Potential Multi-User Setup Detected

     * channels.telegram.groupPolicy="open"
   - Runtime/process tools exposed without full sandboxing in at least one context
   - Current trust model: personal assistant (one trusted operator), not hostile multi-tenant
   - Fix: If mutually untrusted users, split trust boundaries (separate gateways + credentials, ideally separate OS users/hosts)

4. Extension Plugin Tools Reachable Under Permissive Policy

   - Fix: Use restrictive profiles (minimal/coding) or explicit tool allowlists excluding plugin tools for agents handling untrusted input
